title: Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act Provisions; Fisheries of the Northeastern United States; Northeast Multispecies Fishery; Temporary Rule To Extend Fishing Year 2025 Measures
summary:
NOAA has extended temporary rules for the Northeast groundfish fishery through April 30, 2026 to keep the fishery operating while preventing overfishing, and it finalized new gear requirements that tighten how certain gillnets are used and require descending devices for reef fish starting April 1, 2026.

For New England and Mid-Atlantic groundfish, the extension fills a gap while longer-term measures are still under review. It sets catch limits for key stocks so boats can keep fishing, updates sector allocations, and keeps in place restrictions like no keeping Georges Bank cod on recreational vessels and on commercial boats fishing outside sectors. Some programs remain closed and common pool access is limited. The agency says this avoids a shutdown that would have hit vessels, dealers, and coastal communities mid-season, while still cutting overall cod quotas sharply compared to last year to reduce pressure on the stock.

On gear, the rule clarifies gillnet use: exactly sized mesh, one net per vessel, a maximum net length, and floats must stay on the surface with the net kept well off the bottom and not anchored. Separately, all vessels fishing for or holding reef fish must carry a ready-to-use descending device to return released fish to depth, a step aimed at improving survival when fish are released.

Who benefits: sector vessels and shoreside businesses get continuity and clearer rules; anglers and commercial crews gain more certainty about seasons and limits; and fish stocks benefit from conservative catch levels, protections for cod, and practices that can reduce unintended catch and improve survival of released fish. The gear rules may also help protect seafloor habitat and reduce conflicts with wildlife.

Who may be negatively affected: boats facing lower cod limits and closed or restricted programs will likely see reduced income and fewer trip options, and charter and party boats cannot keep Georges Bank cod. Gillnetters must adjust to stricter mesh, length, and configuration limits, which could mean new costs or changes in how and where they fish. Reef fish anglers and crews must buy and use descending devices and allow time to deploy them.

Overall, the agency is prioritizing keeping the fishery open under tighter, precautionary limits while it finishes longer-term planning, and it is standardizing gear practices to support conservation and fish survival.
